rows.title: Service worker persists authenticated API data and personalised pages in Cache Storage and never clears them on logout
rows.requirement: Web client security and correctness (MASTER PROMPT V4.0 lane A: frontend, BFF proxy, middleware, money handling)
rows.reproduction: Read public/sw.js@1eaeecae7: networkFirst() puts every ok navigation (SHELL_CACHE) and GET /api/proxy/* (DATA_CACHE) in Cache Storage keyed by URL and serves it on fetch failure; the only caches.delete is the activate-handler version cleanup (sw.js:49-53). sync/logout.ts wipes IndexedDB/queue/responseCache/key/trust token only. Not run in a browser.
rows.verifierReason: Unambiguous from code; per-user data survives logout on shared browser. Not in prior-findings.
rows.rootCause: SW cache is not namespaced per user/tenant and is outside the logout wipe path
rows.correctiveAction: - `/api/proxy` GETs: network-only (503 OFFLINE JSON on failure); never written to Cache Storage. Offline reads remain served by the encrypted per-user IndexedDB response cache. - Navigation/static/precache writes gated by `isCacheable()`: ok, not redirected, and not `Cache-Control: no-store|private`. - `CIVITASONE_PURGE` message: deletes all `civitasone-*` caches, re-seeds the public `/offline` fallback only. - `performLogout()` deletes `civitasone-*` caches directly (best-effort) and posts `CIVITASONE_PURGE` to the controlling SW. - `CACHE_VERSION` bumped to `v2`, `DATA_CACHE` removed, so activate evicts v1 caches.

rows.title: CSP connect-src 'self' blocks every browser direct-to-storage presigned upload
rows.requirement: Web client security and correctness (MASTER PROMPT V4.0 lane A: frontend, BFF proxy, middleware, money handling)

rows.verifierReason: Cross-origin PUT under connect-src 'self' is blocked by CSP spec; breaks all direct uploads unless storage is same-origin. Only unrelated storage entries in prior-findings (packages/storage).

Reduced to `URL.origin`, http/https only, invalid values yield nothing. Appended to `connect-src`; no wildcards; no other directive touched.

rows.requirement: Citizen service end-to-end flows, fee/refund/issuance/audit integrity (V4.0 lane G)
rows.reproduction: finance revenue-gl/consumer.ts:92-105: on INVALID_HEAD_CODE it enqueues finance.gl.rejected and returns (acked, no retry). grep for glRejected/gl.rejected consumers: only asset-service f3-consumer.ts:670; citizen-service has none, and payment is already paid with receipt issued. rows.verifierReason: Confirmed; fix touches financial posting/event handling across services.
rows.rootCause: The INVALID_HEAD_CODE branch emitted `finance.gl.rejected` and `return`ed (ack). `finance.gl.rejected` had no citizen subscriber (only asset-service filters on `journalId`).

rows.title: Certificate issuance is decoupled from the application: no approved/paid precondition and the application never reaches 'issued'
rows.requirement: Citizen service end-to-end flows, fee/refund/issuance/audit integrity (V4.0 lane G)
rows.reproduction: issuance/validators.ts applicationId optional; issuance/consumer.ts:101-110 reads application only for notification variables; no approved/paid precondition; citizen.certificate.issued and citizen.document.verified have no subscribers (grep). rows.verifierReason: Confirmed; gating issuance on approval/payment alters statutory workflow.
rows.rootCause: `issuanceApprove` only checked certificate state and maker != checker; the linked application was read solely for notification variables and never updated.
rows.correctiveAction: Inside the existing single transaction (markProcessed + guarded write + audit): when the certificate has an `applicationId`, the application must exist in the tenant and be `approved`; if the service has an active fee schedule with `baseAmount > 0`, a payment with status `paid` / `offline_recorded` (or amount 0 for a full exemption) must exist. rows.title: Appeal filing window is evaluated against a client-supplied decisionDate (never the application's actual decision time); applicationId/ownership not verified
rows.requirement: Citizen service end-to-end flows, fee/refund/issuance/audit integrity (V4.0 lane G)
rows.reproduction: appeal/commands.ts:47-49 assertWithinFilingWindow(new Date(body.decisionDate), windowDays) uses validator field decisionDate (validators.ts:13, only a YYYY-MM-DD regex). domain.ts:59-72 accepts any date whose deadline >= today, including future dates. applicationId (optional) is stored unchecked in consumer.ts:36-45; no lookup/ownership/rejected-status check.
rows.verifierReason: Confirmed; statutory limitation window can be defeated by the filer. Fix is statutory logic.
rows.rootCause: `fileAppeal` fed `new Date(body.decisionDate)` into `assertWithinFilingWindow` and never looked the application up; the date validator only checked the YYYY-MM-DD shape and the window check accepts any future date.
rows.correctiveAction: With an `applicationId`: the application is read (tenant-scoped via RLS plus an explicit tenant check), ownership is asserted (citizens: 404 for non-owners, existence not leaked), it must be `rejected` (else 409 NOT_APPEALABLE), the decision date is the server-recorded rejection time (latest `rejected` status-history row, falling back to the application's updated_at), the client date is ignored, and the appeal is attributed to the application's citizen. Without an `applicationId` (decisionRef-only appeals) the date cannot be verified server-side, so a future date is refused (422 INVALID_DECISION_DATE). Window length is still server-derived.
